title: As on a mountain
hook: live as if on a mountain; here or there matters little (Meditations 10.15)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Marcus on getting to know change. Your line was study change. What did you see changing, when you really looked? Day six hundred seventeen.

People dream of the cabin. The mountain view, the quiet, the place where you'll finally be the calm, wise version of yourself. Back in book four, Marcus noted that people seek retreats in the country, by the sea, in the hills, and said you can retreat into yourself instead. In book ten he comes at the same idea from the other side, with a short, strong instruction. Today: as on a mountain.
screen: `THE CABIN DREAM.` → `RETREAT INTO YOURSELF.` → `AS ON A MOUNTAIN.`

segments.voice: First, the line, in George Long's 1862 translation: “Short is the little which remains to thee of life. Live as on a mountain.” Second, what the mountain means. It makes no difference, Marcus goes on, whether a person lives here or there, as long as they live everywhere in the world as a citizen of one great city. The mountain isn't a place you move to. It's a way of standing: above the noise, seeing far, not tangled in every small quarrel of the town below. Third, living in plain view. Let people see, he says, let them know, a real human being living by nature. And then a hard line: if they can't stand him, let them kill him, because that's better than living the way they live. It's the voice of a man who knew public life could be dangerous, and who wanted to be the same in public as in private. Fourth, why the mountain and not the cabin. The cabin promises you'll be different somewhere else. Marcus says the shortness of life means there's no time to wait for the right setting. The height has to come with you, into the office, the kitchen, the commute. Here or there matters little. What you carry matters a great deal.
screen: `LIFE IS SHORT; LIVE AS ON A MOUNTAIN.` · `HERE OR THERE MATTERS LITTLE.` · `LIVE IN PLAIN VIEW.` · `BRING THE HEIGHT WITH YOU.` · then, large: `AS ON A MOUNTAIN.`

segments.voice: If you can, sit somewhere high or quiet: a top step, a window, a balcony, a hill, or just a corner where the noise drops. Otherwise, close your eyes and picture a mountain ledge. Breathe in the height. From up here, look down at today's small tangles: the email, the argument, the errand. See how small and far away they look. Then remember that you'll carry this view back down with you. The bell holds the time.
George Long, whose translation gives Marcus's instruction: short is the little that remains of life, so live as on a mountain. Today's word.
Your line: here or there matters little. Once today, in the middle of something small and tangled, step up a level in your mind and look down at it. Day six hundred seventeen.

howItsDone: Readers of Marcus often use the mountain as a mental vantage point: in the middle of daily friction they picture the wide view, and try to act as they would from there.

original.note: Greek: a mountain. Marcus asks himself to live as on one.

trapdoor: what you thought: go somewhere peaceful.
what it means: bring the mountain's height and distance with you wherever you are, because life is short.
what a scholar hears: the world as one city, one polis, is a Stoic theme; for Marcus it's why here or there matters so little.

notes: Confirm Long's wording of 10.15: 'Short is the little which remains to thee of life. Live as on a mountain.'

10.15 continues: no difference whether here or there if one lives everywhere as in a state (political community); let men see a real man living according to nature; if they cannot endure him, let them kill him, for that is better than to live thus. Paraphrased, including the hard line. A Keeper may wish to soften or cut it.
